title: Trace-guided ingest brokering with retention hints and external annotator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Bursty, high-cardinality logs (debug traces, user-level diagnostics) cause disproportionate hot storage and read amplification in our Loki clusters. Customers see elevated costs and occasional latency spikes when request-scoped debug logs are written alongside regular production telemetry. Current heuristics (tenant-level sampling + static retention policies) are insufficient to route short-lived diagnostic traces to cheaper cold paths without losing critical correlation ability for post-incident investigation.

Proposal: Implement a trace-guided ingest broker that assigns lightweight retention hints to incoming structured log events based on a short-lived external annotator service. The annotator evaluates sampled trace metadata (trace_id, span_type, sampling_decision, error_flag) plus contextual signals (route, model, tenant tier) and emits a retention_hint tag (hot|warm|cold|ephemeral|indexable) and an optional keep_ttl. The ingest broker will: 1) attach retention_hint to the structured log envelope, 2) route events to either fast Loki hot-path or a compacted cold pipeline (Parquet-backed lake) via our existing fanout, and 3) maintain a trace-index manifest in Redis to allow on-demand rehydration (promote cold events to hot for targeted trace replay).

Goals: reduce hot-store token and query pressure by 30% for non-actionable debug traces, preserve cross-request correlation for investigated traces, add minimal end-to-end latency (<10ms p50 added), and provide explicit retention controls that map to cost buckets in Console.

Scope: ingress proxy changes (schema enrich + routing), annotator service (stateless HTTP scorer with simple rules and ML toggle), routing policies in fanout, storage adapters for cold path, rehydration API for Console/Playbooks, and new dashboarding plus SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Retention_hint tag is present on >=99% of structured logs emitted by instrumented services within 5 minutes of rollout.
End-to-end added latency from client write to store decision p50 < 10ms, p95 < 30ms in Canaries.
Hot-store write volume for debug-level logs decreases by >=30% in the staged tenants without loss of trace correlation for flagged investigations.
Rehydration API can promote a trace_id cohort from cold path to hot within 90s and make it queryable in Loki for at least 1 hour.
Console shows cost bucket breakouts by retention_hint and an alert if >5% of events are tagged ephemeral unexpectedly.
Automated tests for schema enforcement, fallback routing, and annotator timeouts are included in the CI pipeline.
Design doc and runbook published to Confluence; at least one on-call rotation reviewed the rollback steps.
technical_notes: Annotator is intentionally stateless: accepts a minimal JSON payload (trace_id, tenant_id, span_meta, hints) and returns retention_hint + optional keep_ttl + confidence_score.
Default policy: annotator timeout = 50ms; on timeout, ingest proxy assigns last-known tenant policy (hot for high-tier, warm otherwise) and emits metric ingest.annotator.timeout.

Routing implementation will leverage existing fanout layer: add a retention_hint header to the envelope so downstream adapters (loki-writer, parquet-sink) can make deterministic routing decisions without shape changes.

Rehydration: maintain a bounded Redis manifest keyed by trace_id -> list of chunk-refs (cold blob pointers). Promote triggers copy from cold store to hot Loki using batch reingest process; reingest respects original timestamps and maintains original trace/span IDs.
Indexing: indexable hints will still write a compact index (trace_id + key fields) to ElasticSearch for fast lookup, even if full payload goes to cold path.
Security: retention_hint metadata is non-sensitive; annotator will not inspect payload bodies. If a tenant opts out, proxy will tag all events as hot and log opt-out metric.

Observability: add metrics ingest.broker.route.{hot,warm,cold,ephemeral} and annotator.confidence buckets; tracing hooks must propagate parent trace context through annotator calls to preserve continuity.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): enable on infra and selected low-throughput dev tenants; monitor latency impact and route metrics; duration 2 weeks.
Stage 2 (Beta): enable for SRE and internal prod staging namespaces; validate rehydration and cost delta; duration 1 week.
Stage 3 (Gradual): progressive percentage rollout by tenant tier with circuit breaker if ingest.broker.route.hot increases >10% unexpectedly.
Stage 4 (GA): expose retention_hint controls in Console per-tenant and add audit logs for annotator decisions.
dashboards_and_alerts: New Console dashboard: Ingest Retention Overview (time series of route distribution, per-tenant heatmap, annotator timeouts).
Latency SLO: ingest.broker.latency.p95 < 50ms; alert if breached for 10m.
Cost Alert: Console alert if hot-store write GB/day for debug logs does not decrease after expected window post-rollout.
Error Alert: if rehydration success rate < 95% over 1h window, page on-call.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for annotator scoring rules and ML toggle behavior.
Integration test: end-to-end ingest from SDK -> proxy -> annotator -> fanout -> cold sink with synthetic traces; assert rehydration path works.
Load test: simulate bursty debug traffic and validate that fanout routing keeps hot store write throughput within target SLOs and that p95 write latency remains stable.
Chaos test: force annotator timeouts and verify fallback policy and metrics.

decision_log: 2026-03-11: Deterministic-first approach approved by Eng Leads; ML scoring behind feature flag.
